critical_issues: 3-year initial term with 180-day termination notice requirement
Auto-renewal for 1-year terms with 120-day notice (4 months)
Buyer may source from alternate supplier and charge price difference for late delivery
24-month warranty period for manufacturing components is long
Supplier liable for product defects causing injury (could be catastrophic)
Buyer indemnifies Supplier for finished product claims except Supplier defects
Joint ownership of improvements creates IP complications
Net 60-day payment terms (Supplier finances Buyer's operations for 2 months)
FOB Supplier's facility means Buyer bears shipping risk
strengths: Liability capped at 12 months fees ($800K-1.2M depending on volume)
Mutual indemnification with appropriate scope division
Price increases capped at 8% annually with 90-day notice
Right to inspect Supplier facilities twice annually
Tooling owned by Buyer (important for sourcing flexibility)
supplier_perspective_risks: Net 60-day payment creates significant cash flow burden
Liability cap still exposes Supplier to $800K-1.2M
Buyer can source alternate suppliers and charge difference if 14+ days late
Exclusive supplier status but no volume guarantee
Joint IP ownership on improvements limits future use
Buyer owns all tooling despite Supplier storing it
24-month warranty is long for manufactured components
buyer_perspective_risks: Auto-renewal with 120-day notice requirement (easy to miss)
Indemnifies Supplier for finished product claims
FOB Supplier means Buyer pays shipping and bears transit risk
Only 10 business days for inspection (tight for complex components)
Price increases up to 8% annually (compounds over 3 years)
6-8 week lead time may be inadequate for JIT manufacturing

warranty_analysis.scope: Free from defects in materials and workmanship, meets specifications
warranty_analysis.remedy: Repair or replacement at Supplier's option (Supplier controls remedy)
warranty_analysis.assessment: 24 months is long for automotive components; creates extended liability exposure

supplier_indemnifies: Product defects causing injury or property damage
indemnification_analysis.assessment: Reasonably balanced but Supplier's product liability exposure is significant
indemnification_analysis.concern: Determining whether injury stems from Supplier defect vs. Buyer design could be litigious

payment_terms_analysis.assessment: Net 60 is aggressive; standard for large buyers but burdensome for suppliers

quality_control_requirements: Buyer inspection rights twice annually with 14 days notice
Assessment: Rigorous QC appropriate for automotive but creates compliance burden
delivery_and_logistics: FOB Supplier's facility (Buyer pays shipping and bears risk)
Late delivery penalty: Buyer may source alternate and charge difference
Assessment: FOB terms favor Supplier but late delivery penalty is punitive
ip_and_tooling: Buyer retains all IP in drawings and specifications
Buyer owns custom tooling (Supplier stores it)
Upon termination, Supplier ships tooling at Buyer's expense
Assessment: Joint IP ownership on improvements will cause disputes; should be clearer
termination_provisions: Buyer may place 6-month inventory orders during wind-down
Assessment: Long notice periods create inflexibility

insurance_requirements.assessment: $5M product liability reflects automotive industry risks

supplier_perspective.product_liability_risk: Potentially millions if components cause injuries

rationale: This contract has balanced elements but several problematic provisions. The 24-month warranty, net 60-day payment terms, joint IP ownership, and significant product liability exposure create risk. The 3-year term with 180-day termination notice and 120-day auto-renewal notice requirements create inflexibility. However, liability caps, mutual indemnification structure, and force majeure protections are reasonable.
required_changes: Reduce warranty period to 12-18 months for automotive components
Improve payment terms to net 45 days (compromise from 60)
Clarify IP ownership - either Buyer owns improvements or they remain with creator
Reduce termination notice from 180 to 90 days
Reduce auto-renewal notice from 120 to 60 days
Add volume commitments or forecasts if Supplier is 'exclusive'
Clarify inspection procedures and acceptance criteria
Add liability allocation for defect vs. design causation
Increase early payment discount to 3% for net 10 to incentivize faster payment
acceptable_for: Established suppliers with strong cash flow, adequate insurance, ISO certification, and experience in automotive industry
